Ṣoḍaśin
------------------------------------------
Among the वेदिच् सच्रिड़िचेस्, those that use the सोम juice for offering as oblations are called Somayāgas.
Out of the seven Somayāgas, the षोडशिन् is the fourth. It is performed to attain vigour.
While extracting the सोम juice from the cuttings of the plant, sixteen śastras (mantras which are to be chanted and not sung) and sixteen stotras (verses taken from the Ṛgveda and set to the musical tunes of Sāmaveda) are used. Hence the name षोडशिन् (comprising sixteen chants).
This is done during the third extraction (= tṛtīyasavana) in the evening.
A quadrangular cup made of khadira wood (Acacia catechu) is used to keep the सोम juice.
Indra is the chief deity appeased through this sacrifice.
See also SOMAYĀGA and VEDIC SACRIFICE.

ṣoḍaśa-saṁskāras
(‘sixteen sacraments’)
------------------------------------------
According to हिन्दुइस्म्, a human being is purified and refined by under-going certain rites, generally called सṁस्कारस्. (See SAṀSKĀRAS.)
The most widely accepted number of such सṁस्कारस् is ṣoḍaśa or sixteen. Hence the name षोडश-सṁस्कारस्.
The Hindu scriptures do not consider birth as the starting point of life. It goes farther back, as it is conditioned by heredity, parentage and environment. Keeping this in मिन्द्, the सṁस्कारस् start with conception.
The following is a brief description of these sixteen सṁस्कारस्:
1. Garbhādhāna
This is mainly concerned with the purification of the seed and the womb so that the progeny will be endowed with good health and intelligence.
2. Puṁsavana
This is performed with the specific desire of getting a male offspring. The pregnant woman is made to undergo this during the third or the fourth month of pregnancy.
3. Sīmantonnayana
This consists in the parting of the hair above the forehead ceremonially. It is said to protect the baby in the womb.
4. Jātakarma
This is performed immediately after the baby is born and before the umbilical cord is cut.
5. Nāmakaraṇa
This is the naming ceremony. It is generally performed on the eleventh or the twelfth day after birth.
6. Niṣkramaṇa
During the fourth month, the baby is brought out of the होउसे (for the first time) where it was born and is blessed by the relatives and friends.
7. Annaprāśana
Performed after the sixth month, this sacrament of feeding the baby with solid ड़ोओद् is primarily meant to wean it away from breast-feeding and gradually get used to normal ड़ोओद्.
8. Cūḍākarma
This is the first hair-cutting ceremony for the male child performed generally during the third year (and before the seventh). A śikhā (tuft of hair) is to be kept.
Vidyārambha or the beginning of primary एदुचतिओन् by teaching the alphabet is a subsidiary rite.
9. Upanayana
This is of primary importance in the life of a द्विज (the twice-born). Investiture with the यज्ञोपवीत (sacred thread) and imparting the गायत्री-मन्त्र are the most important steps.
10 to 13 Vedavratas
A ब्रह्मचारिन् had to undergo four वेदव्रतस्: mahānamnī, महाव्रत, upaniṣadvrata and godānavrata.
They were to be observed after the उपनयन ceremony and for a period of one year each.
Gradually they went out of use and were substituted by other सṁस्कारस् as described later under 16.
14. Samāvartana
This signifies the return of the ब्रह्मचारिन्, after the completion of his studenthood—he is now called a snātaka—to his होउसे.
15. Vivāha
Through विवाह or मर्रिअगे, the स्नातक enters into the second stage of life viz., गार्हस्थ्य (life of the householder). This stage is considered all-important, since the householder is the prop of the whole society.
16. Antyeṣṭi
This stands for all the post-death ceremonies performed by the survivors of the dead-person for his future welfare.
In later dharmaśāstra literature, the four वेदव्रतस् were omitted and the following four were added: कर्णवेध (piercing the ear-lobes); विद्यारम्भ (same as अक्षराभ्यास, learning the alphabet); वेदारम्भ (first study of the वेदस्); केशान्त (cutting the hair or shaving the beard).
See under each title for details.

ṣoḍaśākṣarī-mantra
------------------------------------------
By adding the letter ‘śrīṁ’ to the pañcadaśākṣarīmantra, the षोडशाक्षरी-मन्त्र is generated. It is a very powerful मन्त्र of ललिता-त्रिपुरसुन्दरी, an aspect of the देवी (Divine मोथेर् पार्वती). It has to be received ceremonially from a qualified गुरु.
See also मन्त्र">PAÑCADAŚĀKṢARĪ and TANTRAS.
